# SimLab

> Interactive science simulations: free, hands-on experiments with sliders, live graphs and sound that run in any browser (phone or desktop). Each simulation includes a Learn panel with the concept, formulas, examples and challenges.

<!-- GENERATED by tools/check.mjs --write from assets/js/catalog.js. Do not edit by hand. -->

Source code: https://github.com/i2003-byte/i2003-byte.github.io
Maintainers (human or AI): read AGENTS.md and README.md in the repository first.

## Physics

Launch projectiles, swing pendulums and explore the rules that govern everything from falling apples to orbiting planets. Change the parameters and watch the physics respond instantly.

### Mechanics

- [Projectile Motion](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/projectile/): Launch a ball at any angle and speed. Trace its parabola and measure time of flight, maximum height and range. (Beginner)
- [Simple Pendulum](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/pendulum/): Swing a pendulum, add damping and watch energy flow between kinetic and potential. See how the period depends on length and gravity. (Intermediate)
- [Speed Race: Distance ÷ Time](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/speed-race/): Race two vehicles down a straight track. Set their speeds in km/h, convert to m/s and predict who wins using time = distance ÷ speed. (Beginner)
- [Distance–Time Graph Builder](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/distance-time-graph/): Plan a four-leg bus trip and watch its distance–time graph being drawn. Steep lines mean fast, flat lines mean stopped. (Beginner)
- [Pendulum Clock Lab](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/pendulum-clock/): Time a simple pendulum with a stopwatch, find its time period T = time ÷ oscillations, and fill an observation table to test length and bob mass. (Beginner)
- [Pressure = Force ÷ Area](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/pressure-area/): Rest a brick on sand on its largest, long or smallest face and stack more bricks. See how the same force makes more pressure on a smaller area and digs a deeper dent. (Beginner)
- [Balanced and Unbalanced Forces](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/balanced-forces/): Two teams pull a loaded trolley from opposite sides. Change each pull and see when the forces balance, which way the net force acts and how the trolley speeds up or slows down. (Beginner)
- [Pressure in Liquids](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/liquid-pressure/): A bottle with three holes at different depths: the deeper the hole, the greater the pressure (P = h ρ g) and the faster the jet. Change the level, the liquid and the stool height. (Beginner)
- [Friction on Different Surfaces](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/friction-surfaces/): Pull a wooden block across glass, tile, wood, cloth and sandpaper with a spring balance. Find the force needed to start it moving and to keep it sliding. (Beginner)
- [Rolling vs Sliding Friction](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/rolling-vs-sliding/): Let a wooden block and a toy car go down the same ramp on to glass, tile, cloth or sand. Compare how far each runs and see why rolling friction is so much smaller. (Beginner)
- [Ball Bearings and Lubricants](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/ball-bearings-lubricants/): Spin a potter's wheel on a dry pivot, with powder, with oil or on ball bearings. See how long it keeps turning and how much heat friction makes. (Beginner)
- [Spring–Mass Oscillator](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/): Stretch a spring, release the mass and explore Hooke's law and simple harmonic motion. (Beginner, coming soon)
- [Collisions](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/): Smash carts together and compare elastic and inelastic collisions. Is momentum always conserved? (Intermediate, coming soon)
- [Planetary Orbits](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/): Place planets around a star and explore Newton's gravitation and Kepler's laws. (Advanced, coming soon)

### Sound Lab

- [Vibrating Objects](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/vibration/): Strike a tuning fork, pluck a rubber band or hit a drum. Sound only exists while something vibrates — stop the vibration and the sound stops too. (Beginner)
- [Sound Through Solids, Liquids & Gases](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/sound-media/): Race a sound pulse through steel, water and air. Which medium carries sound fastest, and why? (Beginner)
- [Bell Jar: Sound in a Vacuum](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/bell-jar/): Pump the air out of a jar with a ringing bell inside and listen as the sound fades away. Sound needs a medium to travel. (Beginner)
- [Amplitude & Loudness](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/amplitude-loudness/): Turn the amplitude up and down and watch the wave grow taller. Bigger vibrations make louder sounds. (Beginner)
- [Frequency & Pitch](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/frequency-pitch/): Slide the frequency from a deep rumble to a high whistle. See the wave squeeze together as the pitch rises. (Beginner)
- [Oscillation Counter](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/oscillation-counter/): Swing a pendulum, count its oscillations with a stopwatch and calculate the frequency and time period yourself. (Beginner)
- [Voice Box (Larynx)](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/vocal-cords/): Tighten and loosen virtual vocal cords and push air from the lungs to find out how the larynx makes our voice. (Beginner)
- [Inside the Ear](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/human-ear/): Follow a sound wave down the ear canal to the eardrum, the tiny bones and the cochlea, and see how we hear. (Beginner)
- [Who Can Hear It?](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/who-can-hear/): Pick a frequency and find out whether humans, dogs, bats and elephants can hear it. Explore infrasonic, audible and ultrasonic sound. (Beginner)
- [Music or Noise?](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/music-or-noise/): Look at the wave pattern of each sound clip and sort it: is it a pleasant musical sound or an irregular noise? (Beginner)
- [City Decibel Meter](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/decibel-meter/): Point a sound meter at city sounds — from whispers to fireworks — and measure how loud they are in decibels. (Beginner)
- [Quiet the Neighbourhood](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/noise-pollution/): Add trees, silencers and soundproof walls to cut noise pollution around a school, a hospital and homes. (Beginner)
- [Water Glass Xylophone](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/water-xylophone/): Fill glasses with different amounts of water, tap or blow, and tune your own musical scale. (Beginner)
- [Guitar String](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/guitar-string/): Change the length, thickness and tightness of a string and pluck it. Discover what makes a note higher or lower. (Beginner)

### Waves

- [Wave Interference](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/): Two sources, one pond. See constructive and destructive interference patterns form. (Intermediate, coming soon)

### Optics

- [Pinhole Camera](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/pinhole-camera/): Make a pinhole camera: see how light travelling in straight lines forms an upside-down image, and how the box length and hole size change its size, sharpness and brightness. (Beginner)
- [Plane Mirror and Lateral Inversion](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/plane-mirror/): Drag an object and your eye in front of a plane mirror. See why the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, where the image forms, and why AMBULANCE is written backwards. (Beginner)
- [Newton's Colour Disc](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/newtons-disc/): Spin a disc painted with the seven colours of the rainbow and watch them merge into a whitish grey. Try other colour pairs and find out how fast the disc must spin to fool your eye. (Beginner)
- [Ray Optics](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/): Bend light with lenses and mirrors. Find focal points and form images. (Beginner, coming soon)

### Electricity & Magnetism

- [Electric Circuits and Symbols](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/electric-circuit/): Build a battery, switch and bulb circuit, then redraw it with circuit symbols. See why a bulb lights only in a closed circuit. (Beginner)
- [Heating Effect and the Fuse](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/heating-fuse/): Switch on appliances in a 220 V house circuit and watch the fuse wire heat up. Overload it or cause a short circuit and see the fuse melt to keep the house safe. (Beginner)
- [Make an Electromagnet](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/electromagnet/): Wind wire round an iron nail, connect a battery and pick up pins. Change the turns, cells and core, and watch a compass needle turn. (Beginner)
- [Charging by Rubbing](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/charging-by-rubbing/): Rub a balloon on hair, a comb through dry hair or a glass rod with silk. Watch electrons move, pick up paper bits and push or pull a charged balloon. (Beginner)
- [Gold-Leaf Electroscope](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/electroscope/): Bring a charged rod near an electroscope, touch the cap or earth it with your finger. See charges move and the gold leaves open and close. (Beginner)
- [Lightning and the Lightning Conductor](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/lightning-conductor/): Watch charge build up in a storm cloud until lightning strikes. Fit a lightning conductor, move a person to safety and time the thunder. (Beginner)
- [Electric Fields](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/): Drop positive and negative charges and visualise field lines and equipotentials. (Advanced, coming soon)

### Thermodynamics

- [Hot and Cold: Temperature](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/hot-and-cold/): Heat water from ice to boiling and watch its particles speed up. Why can’t your hand tell the real temperature? (Beginner)
- [Clinical vs Laboratory Thermometer](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/thermometer/): Take your temperature, then measure hot and cold water. Discover the kink, the range and why a clinical thermometer must never go in boiling water. (Beginner)
- [Conduction: Heat Through a Rod](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/conduction/): Heat one end of a copper, iron, glass or wood rod and watch wax-stuck pins drop as heat travels along it. (Beginner)
- [Convection Currents in Water](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/convection/): Heat a beaker at one corner and drop in a permanganate crystal. Hot water rises, cool water sinks and a current carries the heat. (Beginner)
- [Radiation: Black vs Shiny](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/radiation/): Race black, white and shiny cans in front of a heater. Which colour absorbs heat best, and which cools fastest? (Beginner)
- [Sea and Land Breezes](https://i2003-byte.github.io/physics/sea-land-breeze/): Run a day at the seaside. Land heats and cools faster than water, so the breeze blows from the sea by day and from the land by night. (Beginner)
